title: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
summary: Determine the longest string x that can be repeatedly concatenated to form both str1 and str2, indicating that x divides both strings.
statement: Determine the longest string x that can be repeatedly concatenated to form both str1 and str2, indicating that x divides both strings.
constraints: A divisor string repeated whole times must form both inputs.
Return the longest such string or empty.
hints: Compatible repeating strings commute under concatenation.
When str1+str2 equals str2+str1, their common base length is gcd of lengths.
Commutation proves a shared primitive pattern, and the greatest common length gives its longest whole repetition.
editorial: Commutation proves a shared primitive pattern, and the greatest common length gives its longest whole repetition.

tests.explanation: ABC repeated twice forms the first string and once forms the second.
The strings have no shared repeating base.
